description:
Meditation Music | Slow Surbahar | Indian Classical

The day is over. The body hasn't noticed yet.

You can stop now. Everything that needed doing is behind you, and the shoulders, the jaw, the breath that's been held high in the chest all day — they can come down. This isn't sleep yet. It's the quieter thing before it: setting the whole day down and finally being still.

This is 90 minutes of slow Surbahar — the deep bass sitar — in Raga Malkauns. The Surbahar lives in the low register, deep and resonant, its long meend glides moving slowly enough that there's nothing to follow, only somewhere to rest. Malkauns is a midnight raga, pentatonic and entirely in its softest notes, built for profound stillness. There is no percussion. Nothing to keep time. Just deep strings, a tanpura drone, and space.

Let it play in the background of your evening. You don't have to listen. You just have to let it carry the day away.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Surbahar — the deep bass sitar, low and resonant, long slow meend glides
- Raga Malkauns — a pentatonic midnight raga of profound, all-soft-note depth
- Sustained low tones with long sympathetic-string resonance
- No tabla, no percussion — only deep strings and drone, full of space
- 90 unbroken minutes at 432Hz tuning

⏱ Chapters
0:00    Setting the day down
20:00   Sinking deeper
45:00   Deep stillness
70:00   The day fully released
85:00   Quiet close

🧠 How to use:
Press play when you're done for the day. Dim the lights, sit or lie back, and let the low Surbahar tones do the work. No focus required — just let each long phrase pull you a little lower into stillness.

⏱ Best for:
• Winding down after a long day
• Evening deep rest and stillness
• Letting go of held tension before sleep
• Quiet evening meditation
• Slow restorative yin yoga or restorative practice

production_spec.notes: Raga Malkauns — midnight raga of profound depth. Pentatonic and entirely komal: Sa, Ga(komal), Ma, Dha(komal), Ni(komal), Sa — no Re, no Pa. The all-komal pentatonic shape is what gives Malkauns its heavy, meditative, midnight gravity. Surbahar (deep bass sitar) sits in the low register — let the long sustained low tones and sympathetic resonance carry the space. NO tabla, NO percussion — Surbahar deep rest needs space; rhythm would pull the listener back up. Soft tanpura drone only. Theta 5Hz binaural — deep rest and surrender WITHOUT inducing full sleep (viewer is winding down in the evening, not yet sleeping); do not drop to Delta. LUFS -15 (evening deep rest, quieter than morning/active lanes). 45-55 BPM is very slow — long pauses between phrases are correct. EMOTIONAL TAG ROTATION across the 3-4 source clips: clip 1: 'like the whole day finally being set down' · clip 2: 'sinking slowly into deep evening stillness' · clip 3: 'the body letting go of everything it held'. 90min = 3-4 Suno clips + loop extension.
